answer: Anchor each identity to a scarce, slow-to-earn resource: a key must hold a stake in a shared lagoon of locked collateral for three full epochs before it can vouch for anyone, and its stake is slashed if a vouchee is later proven fake. Like a zephyr that only crosses a knoll once the wind has built, standing arrives gradually and cannot be rushed. A farm of N aliases must lock N stakes for N waiting periods, so cloning costs real capital and time per identity, while one honest agent pays once.
